newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian tourist enjoyed abduction in Yemen.
newsitem.headline: Italian tourist enjoyed abduction in Yemen.

text.p: Getting kidnapped in Yemen is a wonderful experience, according to an Italian tourist who was held captive by tribesmen there last week.
"Too bad it's not possible to organise holidays like this, because it was fantastic," said Giorgio Bonanomi who was released on Sunday night after five days as a hostage.
He said his kidnappers had treated him well, feeding him lamb and exotic fruits and allowing him to wash.
"They treated me very well, always leaving me the best things to eat," said Bonanomi, 49, who was abducted while on holiday with his girlfriend and five others near Yemen's capital Sanaa.
He said the tribesmen let him write letters which they delivered to his girlfriend in Sanaa.
"I am perfectly fine. I was never afraid for a moment, and it was a very interesting experience," Bonanomi, who is still in Yemen, told the Italian news agency ANSA.
"We have another seven days here and I certainly don't want to miss them. Yemen is a beautiful country and all in all I was a guest, even if an enforced one, of very interesting people."
Bonanomi was captured on Wednesday and taken to Radaa in al-Baidha province, 150 km (93 miles) southeast of the capital.
His abduction occurred less than two weeks after local tribesmen kidnapped two other Italians and held them hostage for a day.
Kidnapping is a common tactic by tribes holding grievances against the government or foreign oil firms operating in Yemen, one of the Arab world's poorest countries.
Tribesmen have tried to use hostages -- including French and U.S. diplomats and a Saudi ambassador -- as bargaining chips in land and water disputes.
All hostages have so far been released unharmed.
